content:
IncidentBot: Pager — SEV2: data-plane error spike in us-west-2 for /v1/generate (5xx > 15%) across multiple models. Paging on-call.

Arnold: Ack, I'm the on-call. Looking at kube and logs now.

Arnold: Quick checks — control plane shows all model routes healthy in Console, but metrics show downstream 502/504 from infer-0-*/pods.

Jaya: @Arnold do we have any recent config pushes? I see a deploy earlier that touched routing/variant flags around 13:41 UTC.

Maya: Pulling the control-plane audit log. There was a rollout: `feature_flag.routing_priority=v2` and `kv_invalidate=auto` at 13:40:58 UTC.

Thor: I can repro from my laptop: curl to the Console API returns 200 and JSON of routes, but direct data-plane endpoints return 502. Example: `curl -sS -D - https://dp-usw2.infer.redwood/v1/generate -o /dev/null` -> 502.

Lin: Logs from infer-0-12 show repeated "upstream read timeout" and then `503 Service Unavailable` from the local proxy.

Arnold: Hypothesis 1: config was updated in control plane but didn't propagate to all data-plane nodes — some still using old routing table causing incorrect backend selection -> timeouts.

Maya: Adding hypothesis 2: KV cache invalidation raced with the routing change; some nodes cleared their prefix cache and ended up with empty route entries.

Jaya: Dumping relevant logs (snippets):
```
[13:42:10] proxy: selected backend "model-v2" -> connect timeout
[13:42:12] worker: kv_lookup key=routes/usw2 returned null
[13:42:13] proxy: upstream read timeout after 10s
```

Thor: I see in the control-plane audit that the push finished and returned 200 to the deploy job, but the propagation-worker status shows retries on 10% of targets.

Arnold: Mitigation plan: 1) Route new traffic to dedicated fallback pool (dedicated-usw2-fallback) 2) Temporarily rollback routing_priority to v1 3) Force kv cache warmup on remaining nodes.

Jaya: I'll flip routing to fallback and rollback priority to v1. Doing a canary first (10% traffic).

DevExBot: Action taken: traffic-split updated — 90% -> standard, 10% -> dedicated-usw2-fallback by Jaya at 13:44:02 UTC.

Lin: After 30s, error rate dropped from 18% -> 6% on canary.

Maya: Pushing a targeted cache-warm job to the 12 affected data-plane pods now: `kubectl exec -n infer dp-*/ -- /opt/bin/warm_kv routes --region=us-west-2`. Started at 13:45:20.

Thor: Confirmed warmup succeeded on dp-0-03 and dp-0-07. Logs show `routes loaded: 543 entries`.

Arnold: Rolling the routing_priority flag back to v1 globally. Jaya, make the change and monitor.

Jaya: Rolled back routing_priority -> v1 at 13:46:55 UTC. Propagation status shows 97% success after retry.

Maya: Observability notes: Console UI previously showed the new routing table immediately after the control-plane push — which made it look like everything was fine. The data-plane agents didn't confirm applied state in that UI. So Console vs actual dataplane divergence was confusing the initial triage.

Arnold: Good call. That's a control-plane vs data-plane visibility gap. For communications: mark customer impact window starting 13:41 -> 13:47 UTC. Impact: increased 5xx for hosted API in us-west-2, affecting ~120 customers with degraded latency and failed requests.

Lin: Customer support: created incident ticket INC-1298 and sent proactive emails to top-10 affected accounts.

Thor: After rollback + warmup + traffic-split, 5xx fell to baseline (~0.5%) at 13:48:10 UTC.

Arnold: Declaring mitigated at 13:48:30 UTC. Will not close until we confirm stable for 1 hour.

Maya: Next-step follow-ups for RCA:
- timeline reconstruction (pull full audit logs + propagation-worker traces)
- confirm why propagation-worker did retries (OOM? network flaps?)
- add explicit dataplane applied-state check in Console before marking push as complete
- improve runbook: automated fallback to dedicated pool when propagation failure > 5%

Jaya: I'm taking owner for the immediate RCA draft. I'll collect logs and timeline and share in this thread. Assigning ticket: RCA-217.

Arnold: Handoff note: Jaya -> Maya for follow-ups after my shift ends in 25m. Please keep me in loop for high-level notes.

DevExBot: Reminder: create a postmortem skeleton at /docs/incidents/RCA-217 and include timeline + mitigations.

Lin: Logging snippets and the list of affected pods I'm uploading to the ticket.

Maya: Quick outstanding question: was there any correlated autoscaler activity that could have coincided? I'm seeing a k8s node bounce at 13:41:57 UTC that affected 2 pods. Adding to hypotheses.

Arnold: Good, add that to RCA. Closing the live paging loop now. If errors spike again, page the on-call. Thanks all for the quick response :thumbsup:

Jaya: Noted. Will post the initial RCA draft in ~2h.

Thor: Thx — great coordination.

(Incident thread locked for edits to preserve timeline)
